_comment: Golden LLM response fixture for the travel domain. Hand-built against PlanResult, TravelData, SynthesisResult — a valid per-stage output set for a 3-day Kyoto itinerary video. Travel forbids quiz_arena, so no quiz call runs and enrichment_response is null. Drift canary consumed by tests/test_llm_response_fixtures.py.

spots.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
spots.description: Arrive before 7am to walk the torii gates without crowds; the full loop takes about two hours.
spots.tips: JR Nara line to Inari station, 150 yen from Kyoto station

spots.name: Kiyomizu-dera
spots.description: Hillside temple with the wooden stage view over the city; the approach streets are good for lunch.
spots.tips: Bus 206 from Inari area, 230 yen flat fare

spots.name: Gion at dusk
spots.description: Walk Hanamikoji street around 5pm when lanterns come on; keep cameras down near private teahouses.

tips: Buy a 700 yen one-day bus pass at the station kiosk — it pays off after three rides

spots.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
spots.description: Short but iconic path; pair it with the riverside walk to make the trip out worthwhile.
spots.tips: JR Sagano line to Saga-Arashiyama, 240 yen

spots.name: Tenryu-ji
spots.description: Zen garden that predates the buildings around it; the garden-only ticket is enough.

tips: The monkey park climb is steep — skip it in summer heat

spots.name: Nishiki Market
spots.description: Breakfast crawl: tamagoyaki, soy milk doughnuts, and pickles — most stalls open by 9:30.

spots.name: Kinkaku-ji
spots.description: The golden pavilion — a fixed one-way route, so photos are easy even when busy.
spots.tips: Bus 205 from the market area, 230 yen

tips: Ship luggage ahead to the airport with takkyubin (~2000 yen) and ride the train unencumbered

breakdown.notes: Market breakfasts, convenience-store dinners, one sit-down ramen
Two bus day-passes plus JR hops
Souvenirs and the inevitable vending machines

accommodationTips.text: Stay east of the river in Higashiyama — you can walk to day-one temples and skip two bus rides
Hostel curfews still exist in Kyoto; check before booking if you plan late Gion walks

transportationTips.text: Buses take IC cards but the one-day paper pass is cheaper at 3+ rides
Taxis from the station after midnight run 2000+ yen — time your last bus

extraction_response.bestSeason: Late November for autumn color, or the last week of March for early blossoms

synthesis_response.tldr: A costed 3-day Kyoto plan — eastern temples, Arashiyama, and markets — for about 21,500 yen all-in.
keyTakeaways: Base yourself in Higashiyama and walk to day-one temples
The 700 yen bus day-pass beats IC fares after three rides
Go to Fushimi Inari before 7am and Gion at dusk
synthesis_response.masterSummary: Three themed days in Kyoto: temples of the east with an early Fushimi Inari start, Arashiyama's bamboo grove and Tenryu-ji garden, then Nishiki Market and Kinkaku-ji — with a full 21,500 yen budget breakdown, bus-line details for every spot, a packing list, and season advice.
synthesis_response.seoDescription: Budget 3-day Kyoto itinerary with exact costs, bus routes, packing list, and the best times to visit each spot.
